title: Your Side Still Stays Yours
one_line_concept: A complete room still feels khaali because one partner's sense of home lives in one specific person; the story must prove that absence through kept space, familiar corners, and the safety of shared silence.
exact_slide_1_text: khaali hai jo tere bina, main woh ghar hoon tera
creator_provided_slide_2_text: Some people don't just enter your life, they become the place your heart keeps returning to. Without them, even the most familiar corners feel empty. And with them, even silence feels safe. That is the real ache of Ghar - not just missing someone, but realizing that your sense of home was never a place. It was always that one person.
first_frame_visual: One partner alone in a shared room, sitting only on their usual half of the sofa or bed while the other half stays open.
payoff_frame: Same frame, same place, the missing person finally in the kept spot. The room feels full without a dramatic hug.
why_it_wins: The idea makes the lyric physical through a real behavior: not taking the other person's place.
The repaired text has the correct ache, but likely needs story-led splitting to avoid becoming a quote-card wall of text.
The share trigger is clear: send this to the person whose place is still theirs.
The visual stays identity-safe and readable for later prompt work.
